purpose: Bounded randomized beneficiary episode from consumer-directed Medicaid support to service use, unmet need, satisfaction, and health/safety outcomes, kept separate from the informal-caregiver follow-up unit.

events.geography: United States; Arkansas, Florida, and New Jersey Medicaid demonstration
events.date_precision: study-period reference date; beneficiary outcomes were measured around nine months after random assignment with state-specific implementation windows
events.denominator: Adult and other eligible Medicaid beneficiaries enrolled in the three-state randomized demonstration; state enrollment counts and outcome universes vary by report and measure
events.method: ASPE/Cash and Counseling randomized treatment-control comparisons using beneficiary or proxy interviews, service-use measures, unmet-need reports, satisfaction, and health/safety outcomes
events.missingness: Individual identifiers, precise allowance receipt/spending, caregiver linkage, recipient task-level need, long-run health, household finances, provider switching, trust, action, and exit are not retained in this compact record
events.exposure: An eligible Medicaid beneficiary was randomly assigned to direct personal assistance through a monthly allowance and counseling or to receive usual agency-based personal care/home-and-community services
events.alternatives_before_action: Usual agency services, consumer-directed hiring, family care, paid home care, assistive devices, and non-use were possible routes; individual alternative quality and constraints are not fully retained
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Consumer direction increased control over who provided care, when care occurred, and what supportive goods/services were purchased
events.choice_or_response: Treatment beneficiaries could manage an allowance, hire preferred caregivers including family, purchase permitted goods, and use a representative or fiscal/counseling support
events.person_or_actor_with_control: The program established the allowance and safeguards; the beneficiary or representative controlled service direction within eligibility and program rules
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Medicaid consumer direction supplied an implemented alternative to traditional agency-based service delivery
events.remedy_receipt: Random assignment and study follow-up are observed at study level; individual allowance receipt, spending, and completed care are not all verified in this compact record
events.durability_followup: The main follow-up is approximately nine months; longer-term care continuity, health, household security, and recurrence remain open
events.immediate_outcome: Treatment beneficiaries reported greater satisfaction with supportive services, fewer unmet personal-care needs, and increased access to paid home care in the studied comparisons
events.protected_outcome: The intervention protected reported service satisfaction and care access without evidence in the cited summaries of compromised health or safety
events.sacrificed_outcome: Administrative responsibility, hiring/payroll burden, uneven provider availability, and residual unmet need could remain; the summaries do not show that all burdens disappeared
events.cost_risk_transfer: Consumer direction shifts some service-selection power to the beneficiary but can also transfer coordination, hiring, and care-management work to the beneficiary or family
events.later_outcome: Short-run beneficiary service and health/safety outcomes are reported; long-run independence, caregiver durability, household resources, trust, action, switching, and exit are not
events.meaning_and_attribution: Satisfaction is observed, but broader fairness, dignity, institutional legitimacy, and attribution are not retained as a cultural-response endpoint
events.public_or_collective_response: No political or collective response is measured
events.counterexample: A program can improve service satisfaction and reduce unmet need without proving long-run health recovery, caregiver sustainability, or household financial security
events.source_and_uncertainty: ASPE Cash and Counseling reports on beneficiary satisfaction, unmet need, personal care, wellbeing, and health/safety; randomized assignment supports treatment contrasts, while state-specific implementation and outcome universes differ

arrows.evidence: ASPE describes random assignment to individual budgets/counseling versus traditional services and reports increased access to paid care and beneficiary control
arrows.counterexample: Treatment assignment does not mean equal allowance receipt, use, or ability to hire workers across states
arrows.remaining_gap: Take-up, spending, plan completion, provider availability, and individual service continuity

arrows.to: greater service satisfaction and fewer unmet care needs
arrows.evidence: ASPE reports higher satisfaction with supportive services and fewer unmet personal-care needs for treatment beneficiaries in the cited comparisons
arrows.counterexample: The effect varies by state, age, disability, service type, and outcome universe
arrows.remaining_gap: Individual effect sizes, unmet-need type, completed service, and care adequacy

arrows.to: health and safety not worsened in the studied follow-up
arrows.evidence: ASPE implementation and outcome summaries report similar or better health outcomes and no compromised health or safety in the studied treatment comparisons
arrows.counterexample: Short follow-up and study-specific measures do not establish long-run health, safety, or independence for every beneficiary
arrows.remaining_gap: Long-run clinical outcomes, recipient safety, functional independence, and recurrence

arrows.to: durable household recovery, caregiver sustainability, trust, or exit
arrows.evidence: The cited beneficiary results do not follow the same beneficiary-caregiver household through long-run resources, replacement care, trust, action, switching, or exit
arrows.counterexample: Short-run care satisfaction can coexist with later service loss, caregiver exhaustion, or new household costs
arrows.remaining_gap: Same beneficiary-caregiver linkage, long-run care continuity, household security, trust, action, and exit

boundary: This ledger closes a randomized care-support-to-beneficiary-service-outcome segment and remains separate from the caregiver ledger. It does not establish completed care for every participant, long-run recovery, or a pooled beneficiary-caregiver household result.
storage_boundary: Only published ASPE study-level design and outcome statements are retained; no beneficiary, caregiver, Medicaid, or claims microdata are stored.
